evidence.finding: Existing procedure fixes environment, operation, completion criterion, change class and effective policy; inventories actual deploy/rollback targets and traces directional evidence. It explicitly challenges required co-change with a refuting check.

evidence.finding: Release, runtime and infrastructure views remain distinct. Quantum counts require a declared convention, cohesion and coverage; connected components are only a conservative envelope.
evidence.consequence: Avoids inventing universal counts, confusing synchronous completion with coordinated release, or automatically splitting a shared database.

evidence.finding: Mixed-version evidence, binding approval authority, retained events, feature activation and persistent rollback effects already constrain release conclusions.
evidence.consequence: Technical compatibility cannot waive policy; binary independence cannot establish feature or historical-data rollback safety.

evidence.finding: Object-level data access, actual transaction participation, all/any/quorum dependencies, fallback semantics and warm/cold recovery horizons are explicit.
evidence.consequence: An endpoint, framework annotation, timeout or single-peer outage does not establish broader operational independence.

evidence.finding: Directional co-change and Code Maat symmetric degree use different stated denominators; low volume and absence of data remain uncertainty. Formula matches inspected primary implementation.
evidence.consequence: No metric correction justified; metrics remain leads rather than quality scores or proof of necessity.

sources.version: Software Architecture: The Hard Parts, first edition October 2021; copyright 2022; preview third release August 26, 2022
sources.supports: Quantum combines deployability, functional cohesion, static dependencies and synchronous workflow coupling; static and dynamic coupling describe different relationships.
sources.limitation: Preview ends before the deeper coupling sections. It does not validate graph connected components, this skill procedure, every database example, or other editions. PDF text was extracted and read; screenshot retrieval did not yield an inspectable image.

sources.version: Webpage displayed last updated October 20, 2025; captured content hashed
sources.section: Loosely coupled teams: independent changes, testing and deployment; compatible interfaces
sources.supports: Independent delivery is assessed from actual ability to change, test and deploy with limited outside coordination.
sources.limitation: Guidance supports investigation questions, not a numerical threshold, quantum count formula, or proof that the local method improves agent behavior.

sources.version: Moving master retrieved on consultation date, identified by retained content hash; no release binary executed
sources.supports: Symmetric coupling divides shared revisions by the average revision counts and scales by 100; output conversion uses an integer. Existing 20/10/10 example is about 66.7 percent before conversion.
sources.limitation: Source inspection only; no Code Maat execution or production repository mining. Installed versions and filtering choices still need pinning when used.

sources.version: AWS Builders Library webpage as retrieved; no software version applies
sources.section: Static stability, control/data plane dependencies and recovery
sources.supports: Existing capacity can keep serving under conditions that prevent provisioning or recovery; operating phase and time horizon limit independence claims.
sources.limitation: First-party design account, not a fault test of any user system or an estate-wide availability guarantee.

sources.version: Chris Richardson pattern webpage as retrieved
sources.section: Shared Database: resulting context, benefits and drawbacks
sources.supports: Shared data can create schema/change coordination and runtime interference while providing transactional benefits.
sources.limitation: Pattern mechanisms do not prove that one physical database cluster means common table ownership, mandatory lockstep, or a transaction invariant under unspecified isolation.
